title: Rosalind and the Bakery
premise: Beatrix Sandoval keeps her late grandfather's lighthouse on the Maine coast and writes novels under a pen name, convinced that love is a luxury for people whose lives are already settled. When a snowstorm traps her in the village bakery with Elias Marsh, the man she loved at twenty-three, and his business rival, she is forced to confront the identity she hid behind a pseudonym and the mistake that ended everything. As the storm isolates the town, old letters, a failing bakery, and her grandfather's unfinished logbook pull all three toward honesty. Beatrix finally claims both her name and her heart, choosing Elias not because timing improved but because she stopped waiting for it to.
about_author: Petra Sandoval is the pen name of a former pastry chef who traded early-morning ovens for late-night manuscripts after a decade of feeding a small coastal town. She writes love stories about people who arrive too late and stay anyway.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She tends the lighthouse, mails another manuscript under her pen name, and catalogs reasons she doesn't do second chances. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness shown as a choice she pretends isn't one.

chapters.title: Flour and Salt
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She visits Marisol's bakery for her ritual morning bun and learns the bakery is failing; Marisol asks her to help write something that might save it. Beat: reluctant investment in a place that feels like family.

chapters.title: A Name in Print
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He arrives in town to scout the bakery's building for his restaurant group, carrying guilt about a woman he lost ten years ago. Beat: ambition shadowed by an old wound he won't name.

chapters.title: The Rival at the Door
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She recognizes Elias in the bakery before he recognizes her; she slips out the back rather than be known. Beat: panic revealing how much she still hides.

chapters.title: What the Storm Brought
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The forecast turns; roads close; Marisol locks up with Beatrix and Elias inside overnight by accident of timing. Beat: forced proximity begins under protest.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. By candlelight, Elias realizes who she is. The mistake of their twenties surfaces halfway, then retreats. Beat: the past arrives without permission.

chapters.title: Bread at Midnight
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He bakes badly to fill the silence; Beatrix corrects his technique like no time has passed. Beat: intimacy rekindling through hands, not words.

chapters.title: The Pen Name Problem
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias mentions loving a novel called 'Tidewater' — hers. She says nothing. Beat: dramatic irony tightening around her hidden identity.

chapters.title: Logbook Entries
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Snowbound again, she reads her grandfather's lighthouse log and finds entries about her grandmother's 'second chance' that contradict family legend. Beat: memory as unreliable inheritance.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His rival, Dana Whitfield, calls: if he secures the bakery site, he makes partner. He hesitates for the first time. Beat: ambition meets conscience.

chapters.title: Thaw, Briefly
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A road briefly opens; Elias could leave. He stays to finish a loaf instead. Beat: choice disguised as procrastination.

chapters.title: The Mistake, Part One
chapters.summary: Flashback, Beatrix's POV. Twenty-three years old: she let Elias believe she chose the city over him without telling him about the manuscript rejection that broke her. Beat: the wound explained, not excused.

chapters.title: The Mistake, Part Two
chapters.summary: Flashback, Elias's POV. He answered her silence with silence, marrying the wrong safety. Beat: two people who mistook pride for peace.

chapters.title: Dana Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Roads clear enough for her SUV; she checks into the inn and starts courting Marisol with a better offer. Beat: the antagonist humanized but threatening.

chapters.title: Three at One Table
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Dana, Elias, and Beatrix share an awkward dinner; Dana guesses Beatrix and Elias have history. Beat: triangulation and jealousy Beatrix refuses to admit feeling.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knows
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals she's selling because of her daughter's medical bills, not failure — and that she'd rather sell to someone who loves bread than someone who loves square footage. Beat: stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Deadline in the Snow
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His firm gives him 48 hours post-storm to close or walk away. Beat: external clock starts ticking against internal change.

chapters.title: Tidewater, Aloud
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Reading aloud to pass the evening, she almost quotes her own book verbatim; Elias finishes the sentence from memory. Beat: her secret strains at its seams.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Tour
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Beatrix shows him the lamp room; he confesses he never stopped writing her unsent letters. Beat: vulnerability offered and half-received.

chapters.title: Pieces, Not the Whole
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They nearly kiss; she pulls back, offering friendship 'for now.' Beat: her pattern of lending pieces of herself repeats — and she hates it.

chapters.title: Dana's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana offers Marisol full price plus a job for life; Marisol wavers. Beat: money versus meaning made concrete.

chapters.title: The Rejection Letter
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias finds her old rejection letter tucked in the logbook and understands the mistake at last. Beat: the truth out, anger and grief colliding.

chapters.title: Harsh Light
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He accuses her of hiding behind pen names and lighthouses; she accuses him of only wanting what he can acquire. Beat: midpoint rupture, both right and wrong.

chapters.title: Alone with the Lamp
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She maintains the light through a rough night, talking to her grandfather's memory, deciding invisibility was never safety, just slow disappearance. Beat: turning inward before turning outward.

chapters.title: Elias Walks the Shore
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He drafts the acquisition memo and can't finish it; he rereads Tidewater and sees her in every chapter. Beat: recognition that he fell for the writer first.

chapters.title: Marisol's Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol tells Beatrix she knows who 'Petra Sandoval' is — and asks her to write the story of the bakery before it's gone. Beat: being seen by found family.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She publishes an essay under her real name about the bakery, the storm, and the man she lost twice. Beat: public claim of identity; point of no return.

chapters.title: The Essay Goes Out
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He reads it on his phone outside the inn, then tears up the acquisition memo. Beat: love answering courage with courage.

chapters.title: Dana's Grace Note
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana, reading the essay, withdraws her bid — admitting she wanted the building to prove something to her father. Beat: antagonist becomes ally; theme of identity echoed.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias must still report to his firm; he asks Beatrix to come with him and speak for keeping the bakery independent. Beat: she must risk the whole heart in public.

chapters.title: The Boardroom Storm
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. In the city, Beatrix speaks; the firm rejects the proposal and Elias resigns. Beat: climax of external plot — everything staked and lost.

chapters.title: Empty Hands
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Jobless and uncertain, Elias drives back through fog; Beatrix fears she's cost him everything. Beat: despair before resolution.

chapters.title: The Logbook's Last Page
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She finds her grandfather's final entry: instructions to keep the light 'for whoever comes home late.' She realizes the lighthouse — and she — were always meant as shelter, not fortress. Beat: thematic key turned.

chapters.title: An Offer of Her Own
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol proposes Beatrix and Elias co-own the bakery: his hands, her name, her recipes. Beat: found family builds the bridge neither dared build alone.

chapters.title: Saying Yes Badly
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias fumbles a confession on the bakery doorstep mid-flour-dust; Beatrix laughs and kisses him mid-sentence. Beat: joy earned through imperfection.

chapters.title: Reopening Day
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The bakery reopens as 'Sandoval & Marsh'; the whole town comes; Dana sends flowers. Beat: community as reward for authenticity.

chapters.title: Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Her next novel is announced with her real byline; her editor warns pen-name fans may feel betrayed. She signs it anyway. Beat: identity fully claimed.

chapters.title: First Snow Again
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. One year later, a storm closes the roads again — deliberately this time, the three of them baking together. Beat: the mistake of their twenties transformed into tradition.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the lighthouse, Elias asks what happens when timing fails again; she answers that she'll stay anyway. Beat: thesis resolved — love as staying, not arriving.

chapters.title: Keep the Light
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, epilogue. She lights the lamp, writes the last line of her new book, and watches Elias cross the yard below. Beat: quiet, complete resolution — visible, named, and home.
